meta.title: Biocalibration + 10-20 Electrode Placement Question Harvest
meta.purpose: Copyright-safe original candidate questions harvested from newly reviewed technologist education sources. Review before moving any item into active D2A-D2C banks.
editorialRules: Do not copy source assessment questions or slide wording.
Use source concepts and practical workflows to create original scenarios.
Do not activate version-sensitive numerical specifications from legacy material without current AASM/BRPT verification.
User-facing references should render in APA style; internal source keys and locations are editorial metadata only.

morley-2016.apa: Morley, A., Hill, E., & Kaditis, A. G. (2016). 10-20 system EEG placement [Workshop presentation]. European Respiratory Society.

ers-2015.apa: European Respiratory Society. (2015). Hands-on polysomnography: Educational Skills Workshop 25, 27 [Workshop materials]. ERS Annual Congress, Amsterdam.

questions.prompt: A technologist is measuring two patients with very different head sizes. Why should electrode locations be determined with the 10-20 system instead of being estimated by eye?
options: It places every electrode the same number of centimeters apart on all patients
It uses proportional measurements so placement is standardized for the patient's head size and shape
It eliminates the need to identify anatomic landmarks
It allows electrodes to be placed only over the central region
questions.answer: It uses proportional measurements so placement is standardized for the patient's head size and shape
questions.rationale: The workshop describes the 10-20 system as a standardized method with electrode positions proportional to skull size and shape.

questions.prompt: During hookup, a trainee labels an electrode with the suffix z. What does that designation indicate in the 10-20 naming system?
questions.rationale: The source identifies odd numbers with the left side, even numbers with the right side, and Z with the midline.

questions.prompt: Before measuring electrode positions, which set of landmarks should the technologist identify according to the workshop?
options: Nasion, inion, and the left and right preauricular points
Left mastoid, right mastoid, chin, and sternum
Nasion, vertex, left canthus, and right canthus
questions.answer: Nasion, inion, and the left and right preauricular points
questions.rationale: The 10-20 measurement workflow begins with four skull landmarks: nasion, inion, and both preauricular points.

questions.prompt: A technologist has marked the midpoint of the nasion-to-inion measurement and the midpoint of the left-to-right preauricular measurement. Which electrode site is established where those midpoint markings intersect?
questions.rationale: The workshop locates Cz by aligning the midpoint of the preauricular measurement with the midpoint of the nasion-inion midline measurement.

questions.prompt: The preauricular-to-preauricular measurement over the head is 38 cm. How far from a preauricular point is the first 10% mark?
questions.rationale: The transverse 10-20 sequence begins with a 10% interval. Ten percent of 38 cm is 3.8 cm.

questions.prompt: After the basic 10-20 grid is marked, the technologist needs to locate F3 using the workshop method. Which measurements are used to create the intersecting midpoint marks?
questions.rationale: The source describes locating F3 by marking the midpoint of Fp1-C3 and the midpoint of Fz-F7.

questions.prompt: Where should M1 and M2 be placed in the hookup workflow described in the workshop?
options: On the bony mastoid prominences behind the ears
One centimeter above each outer canthus
questions.answer: On the bony mastoid prominences behind the ears
questions.rationale: M1 and M2 are identified as reference electrodes placed on the mastoid processes, the bony prominences behind the ears.

questions.prompt: A technologist is applying the two EOG electrodes using the workshop's arrangement. Which placement pattern matches the source?
options: Right electrode lateral and above the horizontal; left electrode lateral and below the horizontal
Both electrodes directly above the pupils
Right electrode lateral and below; left electrode lateral and above
Both electrodes on the mastoid processes
questions.answer: Right electrode lateral and above the horizontal; left electrode lateral and below the horizontal
questions.rationale: The source places the EOG electrodes at the outer canthi with a 1-cm vertical offset: right out/up and left out/down.

questions.prompt: Which arrangement best matches the chin EMG setup described in the workshop?
options: One electrode on the mentalis and two on the submentalis
Two electrodes on the mentalis only
One electrode on each mastoid and one on the chin
Three electrodes over the anterior tibialis
questions.answer: One electrode on the mentalis and two on the submentalis
questions.rationale: The workshop describes a three-electrode chin EMG setup with one mentalis and two submentalis electrodes.

questions.prompt: An EEG site has poor electrical contact before lights out. Which preparation step from the workshop most directly addresses oil and dead skin that can interfere with electrode contact?
options: Clean with isopropyl alcohol, then use abrasive paste with a cotton tip
Add a notch filter before checking the electrode
Move the reference electrode to the forehead
Increase display gain without changing the electrode site
questions.answer: Clean with isopropyl alcohol, then use abrasive paste with a cotton tip
questions.rationale: The workshop describes alcohol for removing grease and abrasive paste for removing dead skin cells as part of skin preparation.

questions.task: Perform procedures and follow practice guidelines
questions.prompt: Before lights out, the technologist asks the patient to perform a series of known movements and breathing maneuvers while the signals are observed. What is the main purpose of this calibration sequence?
options: To verify that recorded channels respond appropriately to known patient actions before the study begins
To determine the patient's final sleep stage before lights out
To replace the need for electrode impedance checks
questions.answer: To verify that recorded channels respond appropriately to known patient actions before the study begins
questions.rationale: The workshop labels the sequence as calibration for checking signals and pairs known patient maneuvers with observation of the corresponding channels.

questions.task: Perform procedures and follow practice guidelines
questions.prompt: During calibration, the patient is asked to look right and left without turning the head. Which recording should the technologist primarily evaluate for the expected response?
questions.rationale: Directional eye movements are included in the calibration sequence to check the eye-movement recording.

questions.task: Perform procedures and follow practice guidelines
questions.prompt: The patient follows the instruction to look up and then down several times while keeping the head still. What should the technologist use this maneuver to assess?
options: Whether the EOG channels detect controlled vertical eye movement
Whether the leg electrodes detect dorsiflexion
Whether the snore sensor responds to vibration
Whether the mastoid electrodes are over the bony processes
questions.answer: Whether the EOG channels detect controlled vertical eye movement
questions.rationale: The workshop includes up-and-down eye movement as a specific signal-check maneuver during calibration.

questions.task: Perform procedures and follow practice guidelines
questions.prompt: A patient is instructed to blink five times during the calibration sequence. Which signal family is being challenged with a known physiologic event?
questions.rationale: Five eye blinks are one of the source's calibration maneuvers and provide a recognizable ocular response.

questions.task: Perform procedures and follow practice guidelines
questions.prompt: Which pre-study maneuver from the workshop most directly activates the chin EMG?
questions.rationale: Jaw clenching is included in the calibration sequence and produces muscle activity that can be observed in the EMG channels.

questions.task: Perform procedures and follow practice guidelines
questions.prompt: Why does the workshop have the patient point and flex one foot and then repeat the maneuver with the other foot?
options: To verify the leg EMG responses and preserve left-right identification
To establish the snore channel baseline
To determine the patient's sleep latency
questions.answer: To verify the leg EMG responses and preserve left-right identification
questions.rationale: The source directs the technologist to flex each foot separately and document each leg, allowing the corresponding leg signal to be checked.
questions.sourceLocation: Slide 29: flex foot and document each leg

questions.task: Perform procedures and follow practice guidelines
questions.prompt: During respiratory calibration, the patient breathes normally and then takes a deliberate breath in and out. What additional action does the workshop instruct the technologist to perform?
options: Check polarity and mark inspiration and expiration on the study
Score the maneuver as an apnea
questions.answer: Check polarity and mark inspiration and expiration on the study
questions.rationale: The source specifically instructs the technologist to check polarity and mark IN and OUT during the breathing maneuver.

questions.task: Perform procedures and follow practice guidelines
questions.prompt: The patient is asked to imitate a snore before lights out. Which channel or sensor response is this maneuver intended to check?
questions.rationale: The workshop includes an imitated snore as a calibration maneuver for checking the snore recording.

questions.prompt: The patient repeatedly looks right and left during calibration, but the EOG channels remain essentially flat while the other channels respond normally. What should the technologist investigate first?
options: The EOG electrodes and EOG channel connections
questions.answer: The EOG electrodes and EOG channel connections
questions.rationale: Because the known eye-movement maneuver should be represented in the EOG recording, an absent EOG response localizes the first troubleshooting step to that signal path.
questions.sourceLocation: Slides 26 and 29: EOG placement and calibration

questions.prompt: During a jaw-clench calibration, a burst of high-frequency activity appears in EEG, EOG, and EMG channels. How should the technologist interpret this pattern?
options: As physiologic muscle artifact produced by the jaw clench
As sweat sway caused by low-frequency drift
As an electrode pop caused only by a broken wire
As proof that the patient is in REM sleep
questions.answer: As physiologic muscle artifact produced by the jaw clench
questions.rationale: The hands-on PSG workshop specifically demonstrates jaw clenching during biocalibration producing high-frequency muscle activity in EEG, EOG, and EMG signals.
questions.sourceLocation: PSG Artifact Recognition and Resolution: jaw clenching example

questions.prompt: During calibration, the patient flexes the left foot, but the deflection is recorded in the channel labeled right leg; flexing the right foot appears in the channel labeled left leg. What should the technologist suspect?
options: The leg channels or input assignments are reversed
The patient has developed an arousal disorder
questions.answer: The leg channels or input assignments are reversed
questions.rationale: Testing each leg separately and documenting the maneuver allows laterality errors to be recognized before the study.
questions.sourceLocation: Slide 29: flex each foot and document each leg

questions.prompt: The patient follows the instructed breathing maneuver, but the recorded respiratory deflection is opposite the direction expected by the laboratory convention. Which technical issue should be checked?
questions.rationale: The calibration instructions explicitly pair deliberate inspiration and expiration with checking polarity and marking IN and OUT.

questions.prompt: A channel shows intermittent abrupt transients and the electrode contact is unstable. Which artifact described in the workshop best fits this problem?
questions.rationale: The workshop lists high impedance and poor electrode contact among extrinsic problems associated with electrode popping.
questions.sourceLocation: PSG Artifact Recognition and Resolution: extrinsic artifact

questions.prompt: A slow, low-frequency baseline drift develops as the patient becomes sweaty. Which artifact category from the workshop is the best match?
questions.rationale: The artifact workshop identifies sweat as an intrinsic physiologic source of low-frequency artifact and also discusses sweat sway.
questions.sourceLocation: PSG Artifact Recognition and Resolution: intrinsic artifact and sweat sway

questions.prompt: High-frequency artifact appears at the same time in C3-M2 and O1-M2 while channels that do not use M2 are cleaner. Which electrode should be inspected first?
questions.rationale: The workshop shows an example in which poor contact at M2, shared by both channels, produces high-frequency artifact in C3-M2 and O1-M2.
questions.sourceLocation: PSG Artifact Recognition and Resolution: poor M2 contact example

questions.prompt: A legacy workshop asks the technologist to compare EEG electrode impedance with a specific numerical target. Which value is stated in that 2016 source?
questions.rationale: The 2016 workshop states an EEG impedance target below 5 kOhm. This item is retained only as a source-harvest candidate because current numerical technical specifications must be verified before activation.
questions.verificationNote: Do not activate as a current-standard question until the current AASM scoring manual/technical specifications are checked.

questions.prompt: The 2016 workshop states that the sleep montage should sample EEG activity from which three general regions?
questions.rationale: The legacy workshop states that a minimum of three EEG derivations are used to sample frontal, central, and occipital activity. The concept should be checked against current technical specifications before activation.
questions.verificationNote: Confirm current AASM technical requirements and current BRPT alignment before activating this version-specific montage item.
